Overview

MacroScript is a text language for MacroDroid macros. You write one macro in one .ms file. The compiler converts the file to the MacroDroid export JSON. You then import the JSON on the phone.

This reference covers the language and every command in the MacroDroid LLM Schema v1.0 (MacroDroid 6.0): 124 triggers, 87 constraints and 208 actions. The mapping file macroscript-mapping.json holds the same data in a form that the compiler can read.

The output leaves out optional fields that hold their default value. For example, m_useAlarm is true by default, so the compiler does not write it.

A larger example

How to read a command entry

  • The heading is the MacroScript name. The grey code next to it is the MacroDroid class type.
  • The signature shows the parameters. Bold names are required. A name with ? is optional. An underlined name can be given without its name.
  • The Kind column tells you what to write. See Arguments.
  • The JSON field column shows where the value goes in the output.
  • Parameters that the compiler fills by itself are shown, but you do not write them.

File structure

  • A file holds annotations, then up to four blocks: variables, triggers, constraints and actions.
  • Each block can occur one time only. Any order is permitted. The recommended order is variables, triggers, constraints, actions.
  • A macro file must have a triggers block and an actions block.
  • The variables block and the constraints block are optional.
  • An action block file (@actionBlock) must not have a triggers block or a constraints block.
  • No other top-level code is permitted.

End each statement with ;. Names are case-sensitive. Letters, digits and underscore. The first character must be a letter or an underscore. Names are case-sensitive.

Annotations

AnnotationTargetJSON fieldDefaultDescription
@name(string)filemacro.m_namefile name without .msSets the macro name.
@description(string)filemacro.m_descriptionempty stringSets the macro description. The compiler gives a warning if it is missing.
@category(string)filemacro.m_categoryUncategorizedSets the macro category.
@enabled(bool)filemacro.m_enabledtrueSets the enabled state after import.
@favouritefilemacro.isFavouritefalseMarks the macro as a favourite.
@headingColor(color)filemacro.m_headingColornoneSets the heading color. Use a color literal, for example #FF2196F3.
@noLogfilemacro.m_excludeLogfalseStops all logging for the macro.
@logLevel(FULL | TRIGGERS_ONLY)filemacro.loggingLevelFULLFULL writes 0. TRIGGERS_ONLY writes 1.
@actionBlockfilemacro.isActionBlockfalseCompiles the file as an action block. Triggers and constraints blocks are not permitted.
@disabledstatementitem.m_isDisabledfalseDisables one trigger, constraint or action. Put it before the statement.
@comment(string)statementitem.m_commentnoneSets the comment of one item. A /** */ comment does the same thing.

Put file annotations at the top of the file. Put statement annotations on the line before the statement.

Comments

FormUse
// textComment to the end of the line. The compiler ignores it.
/* text */Comment over many lines. The compiler ignores it.
/** text *//** text */ before a trigger, constraint or action statement. The compiler writes the text to m_comment of that item.

Variables

Declare variables in the variables block. The syntax is the same as a Java declaration.

TypeType codeValue fieldLiteral
bool0m_booleanValuetrue, false
int1m_intValue42, -7
string2m_stringValue"text"
decimal3m_decimalValue1.5
dict4dictionary (isArray false){"key": value, ...}
array5dictionary (isArray true)[value, ...]
color6none. A color variable has no initial value. Assign it in the actions block.#RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB (in assignments only)

Modifiers

ModifierEffectNote
globalRefers to a global variable that already exists on the phone. The compiler does not write it to the root globalVariables array. Magic text uses {v=name}.Create the global variable on the phone (MacroDroid Variables screen) before you import a macro that uses it. An initial value on a global is a compile error. This rule makes sure that an import never changes a value that is on the phone.
secureSets isSecure true.
inAction blocks only. Sets supportsInput true.
outAction blocks only. Sets supportsOutput true.

Rules

  • Declare every variable in the variables block before you use it. This includes global variables that are on the phone.
  • A declaration without a value gets the default: false, 0, empty string, 0.0, empty dict or empty array.
  • A color variable cannot have an initial value. Write color accent; and then accent = #FF2196F3; in the actions block. An initial value is a compile error.
  • A global variable cannot have an initial value. An initial value is a compile error.
  • Local variables compile to macro.localVariables with isLocalVar true. Magic text uses {lv=name}.
  • Dict and array literals compile to the dictionary field: {"entries": [...], "isArray": false or true}. Array keys are the index as a string: "0", "1", "2".
  • Each entry is {"key": "k", "variable": {...}}. The variable object has a type field and one value field: StringValue with textValue, IntegerValue with intValue, DecimalValue with decimalValue, BooleanValue with booleanValue.
  • A nested dict or array is an entry whose variable is {"type": "Dictionary", "entries": [...], "isArray": false or true}. Nesting can go to any depth.

Literals

LiteralExamplesRule
int0 42 -7
decimal0.5 -1.25
string"text" "line\nnext" "Battery: ${sys.battery}%" Escapes: \" \\ \n \t \$
booltrue false
nullnull
duration500ms 30s 5m 2h 1m30sUnits are ms, s, m and h. You can join units: 1h15m. The compiler converts the value to the unit of the parameter. A plain int is also accepted. A plain int uses the unit of the parameter.
color#FF0000 #88FFFF22#RRGGBB gets alpha FF. The compiler writes a signed 32-bit ARGB int. #FFFF0000 becomes -65536.
list[1, 2, 3] [MON, WED, FRI] ["a", "b"]
object{"key": "value"} {key: "value"}Keys can be strings or bare identifiers.
constantTURN_ON SHORT_BUZZ WEEKDAYSConstants are UPPER_CASE. A constant is valid only for the parameter that defines it. You do not import constants.

Day groups

Day constants are the same everywhere. The compiler puts them in the order that the parameter needs. TimerTrigger and SetAlarmClockAction use Mon first. DayOfWeekConstraint uses Sun first.

GroupDays
WEEKDAYSMON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI
WEEKENDSSAT, SUN
EVERY_DAYMON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, SUN

Strings and magic text

MacroDroid fills values into text with magic text, for example {lv=count}. In MacroScript you write ${...} in a string. The compiler writes the magic text.

String literals that go to a parameter with interpolation true, to a string variable, or to a log or notification text.

You writeCompiles to
${name}local: {lv=name} ; global: {v=name}
${name["key"]}local: {lv=name[key]} ; global: {v=name[key]}
${name["a"]["b"]}local: {lv=name[a][b]} ; global: {v=name[a][b]}
${name[0]}local: {lv=name[0]} ; global: {v=name[0]}
${name[k]} where k is a variablelocal: {lv=name[{lv=k}]} ; global: {v=name[{lv=k}]}
${sys.battery}result: {battery}
${key} or ${value} inside for (key, value : d)result: {iterator_dictionary_key} or {iterator_value}. For an array, key gives {iterator_array_index}.
\${result: a literal ${
\{battery}result: the literal text {battery}. The compiler writes \{battery}, which MacroDroid shows as {battery}.

Text in single braces, for example {battery}, goes to the output with no change, so MacroDroid fills it in. This is an escape hatch. Prefer ${sys.battery}.

To show a literal brace, write \{ in MacroScript. The compiler writes \{ only when the text inside the braces is valid magic text (a sys name, v=name or lv=name). In all other cases it writes { with no backslash, because MacroDroid shows a backslash that is not part of an escape.

  • Interpolation in a parameter that does not support magic text is a compile error.
  • ${name} where name is not declared and is not a loop alias is a compile error.

See System values for every sys. name.

Triggers block

Syntax: triggers { trigger(args) [as label] [when (condition)]; ... }

  • Each statement is one trigger. Multiple triggers use OR logic: any one starts the macro.
  • The block must hold at least one trigger. For a macro that you start by hand, write manual(); (EmptyTrigger).
  • 'as label' gives the trigger a name. The compiler gives a labeled trigger a placeholder m_SIGUID (112233445566771, 112233445566772, ...). Use the label in triggeredBy(label).
  • 'when (condition)' adds trigger-level constraints to m_constraintList of that trigger.

Constraints block

Syntax: constraints { condition; ... }

  • Each statement is a condition. All statements must be true (AND).
  • A statement can use &&, || and ! with parentheses.
  • If the block has one statement that is a flat OR (a || b || c), the compiler writes a flat list and sets macro.m_isOrCondition true.
  • Other mixed logic compiles to LogicConstraint items.

Actions block and statements

Syntax: actions { statement; ... }

  • Statements run in order. The compiler writes one flat m_actionList.
  • Braces in if, else and loops become open and close marker actions (IfConditionAction ... EndIfAction, LoopAction ... EndLoopAction).
  • 'when (condition)' after an action call adds action-level constraints to that action only.
StatementCompiles toNote
action(args);One action item with m_classType from the mapping.
action(args) when (condition);The action with m_constraintList set from the condition.
x = value;SetVariableAction
if (c) { } else if (c) { } else { }IfConditionAction, ElseIfConditionAction, ElseAction, EndIfActionExactly one EndIfAction closes each chain. The condition goes in m_constraintList of the If or ElseIf item.
if (confirm(title: "..", text: "..")) { } else { }IfConfirmedThenAction ... ElseAction ... EndIfActionconfirm() must be the whole condition. 'else if (confirm(...))' compiles to ElseIfConfirmedThenAction.
while (c) { }LoopAction m_option 1 (While-Do), condition in m_constraintList, EndLoopAction
do { } while (c);LoopAction m_option 2 (Do-While), EndLoopAction
while (true) { }LoopAction m_option 3 (Endless), EndLoopActionPut a wait() and a break inside, or the loop runs with no delay.
repeat (5) { }LoopAction m_option 0, m_fixedOptionCount 5, EndLoopAction
repeat (count) { }LoopAction m_option 0, m_fixedOptionVariable from the int variable, EndLoopAction
repeat (30s) { }LoopAction m_option 4, timedDurationValue 30, timedTimeUnit 0, EndLoopActionThe compiler uses the largest unit that gives a whole number: s=0, m=1, h=2.
for (key, value : d) { }IterateDictionaryAction {variableName, isArray from the declaration, dictionaryKeys {keys: []}} ... EndLoopActionkey and value are aliases. For a dict: {iterator_dictionary_key} and {iterator_value}. For an array: {iterator_array_index} and {iterator_value}. To walk a nested entry, write for (k, v : d["inner"]); the keys go in dictionaryKeys.
break;BreakFromLoopAction
continue;ContinueLoopAction
return;TerminateRunningActionIt stops only this run of the macro.
wait(2s);PauseAction m_delayInSeconds 21500ms writes m_delayInSeconds 1 and m_delayInMilliSeconds 500. wait(count, MINUTES) uses a variable: m_variable and unitForVariables.
waitFor(trigger(...), timeout: 30s);WaitUntilTriggerAction with the trigger in triggersToWaitForGive a list for more than one trigger: waitFor([a(), b()]). timeout sets timeoutEnabled true. Named arguments: continueOnTimeout, result (bool variable).
callBlock("Block Name", inputs: {in1: x}, outputs: {out1: myVar});ActionBlockActionasync: true sets continueActionsWithoutWaiting. The compiler finds the .ms file with @actionBlock and that @name, compiles it into macro.exportedActionBlocks, and uses one placeholder GUID for both.
raw("ClassName", {json});One item with m_classType ClassName and the given fields, with no checksUse this for a command that the mapping does not have yet. It is permitted in all three blocks.

Assignment

You writeSetVariableAction fields
b = true;m_newBooleanValue true
b = !b;m_booleanInvert true
b = otherBool;m_otherBooleanVariable {m_name, m_type 0, isLocalVar}
i = 5;m_newIntValue 5
i++; or i += 1;m_intValueIncrement true
i--; or i -= 1;m_intValueDecrement true
i += 3;m_intExpression true, m_expression "{lv=i}+3"
i = j * 2 + 1;m_intExpression true, m_expression "{lv=j}*2+1"
i = random(1, 10);m_intRandom true, m_intRandomMin 1, m_intRandomMax 10
d = random(0.0, 1.0);m_intRandom true, m_doubleRandomMin, m_doubleRandomMax (decimal variable)
x = 1.5;m_newDoubleValue 1.5
s = "Hi ${name}";m_newStringValue "Hi {lv=name}"
s += "!";m_newStringValue "{lv=s}!"
s = "a" + name + "b";m_newStringValue "a{lv=name}b"
s = sys.clipboard;m_newStringValue "{clipboard}"
c = #FF0000;m_newStringValue "#FF0000" (color variable). This is the only way to give a color variable a value.
s = prompt(title: "Name?", message: "Type it");m_userPrompt true, m_userPromptTitle, m_userPromptMessage
Other named arguments: password, passwordToggle, emptyAtStart, showCancel, stopAfterCancel, trueLabel, falseLabel.
d["k"] = 5;dictionaryKeys ["k"] (a plain list of strings), dictionaryOrArrayType 1
dictionaryOrArrayType uses the variable type codes: 0 bool, 1 int, 2 string, 3 decimal. Use -1 when the target is not a dict or array entry. A key can be a variable: d[k] = 5 writes dictionaryKeys ["{lv=k}"].
a[0] = "x";dictionaryKeys ["0"]
d = other;copyDictionaryLocation {variableName: "other"} (dict or array only)
  • Every assignment writes m_variable as {m_name, m_type, isLocalVar} from the declaration.
  • Assignment to an undeclared name is a compile error.
  • Type mismatch is a compile error. Use a cast for dictionary entries: i = (int) d["k"];

Conditions

Conditions are used in the constraints block, in if, else if, while and do ... while, and after when.

You writeCompiles to
flagMacroDroidVariableConstraint m_booleanValue true
!flagMacroDroidVariableConstraint m_booleanValue false
i == 5MacroDroidVariableConstraint m_intValue 5
i != 5m_intValue 5, m_intNotEqual true
i > 5m_intValue 5, m_intGreaterThan true
i < 5m_intValue 5, m_intLessThan true
i >= 5int: m_intGreaterThan with 4. decimal: LogicConstraint OR of > and ==.
i > jm_intCompareVariable true, m_otherValueToCompare {m_name j}
i > (j * 2)m_expression "{lv=j}*2" with m_intGreaterThan
x > 1.5m_doubleValue 1.5, m_intGreaterThan true (decimal variable)
s == "a"m_stringValue "a", m_stringComparisonType 0, m_stringEqual true, checkCase true
s != "a"m_stringComparisonType 0, m_stringEqual false, checkCase true
s.equalsIgnoreCase("a")m_stringComparisonType 0, m_stringEqual true, checkCase false
s.contains("a")m_stringComparisonType 1, checkCase true
s.containsIgnoreCase("a")m_stringComparisonType 1, checkCase false
!s.contains("a")m_stringComparisonType 2 (Excludes)
s.matches("^a.*")m_stringComparisonType 0, m_stringEqual true, enableRegex true
d["k"] == 5dictionaryKeys {keys ["k"]}, dictionaryType 1 (from the literal)
(int) d["k"] > idictionaryType 1 from the cast
sys.battery_int > 50CompareValueConstraint type 1, value1 "{battery_int}", value2 "50", comparisonType 3
"${sys.ssid}".contains("Home")CompareValueConstraint type 2, comparisonType 4
d.containsKey("k")CompareValueConstraint type 4 (dict) or 5 (array), value1 "{lv=d}", value2 "k", comparisonType 6. .containsValue(v) uses 8. With ! in front: 7 and 9.
triggeredBy(morning)TriggerThatInvokedConstraint m_siGuidThatInvoked = SIGUID of morning, m_triggerName, m_not false
!triggeredBy(morning)TriggerThatInvokedConstraint m_not true
wifi(wifiState: CONNECTED_TO_SPECIFIC_SSID, ssidList: ["Home"])Any constraint call compiles to that constraint.
a && bFlat list, m_isOrCondition false
a || bFlat list, m_isOrCondition true
a && (b || c)a, then LogicConstraint m_option 1 with children b and c
!constraintCall(...)LogicConstraint m_option 3 (NOT) with one child
xor(a, b)LogicConstraint m_option 2
  • A condition can use constraint calls, variable comparisons, sys comparisons, triggeredBy() and confirm().
  • confirm() is valid only as the whole condition of if or else if.
  • Trigger calls are not valid in a condition. Use the matching constraint. For example use screenOnOff in constraints, not the trigger with the same name.

Arguments

  • Arguments are named: setWifi(state: TURN_OFF).
  • A command can take one argument with no name. The mapping marks it with positional true. Example: setWifi(TURN_OFF).
  • Give named arguments in any order.
  • Leave out an optional argument to use its default.
  • A required argument with no value is a compile error. An argument with usedWhen is required only when that condition is true.
  • An unknown argument name is a compile error.
  • An enum argument also accepts a plain int. Use this only when a constant is missing.

Argument kinds

KindWhat to write
booltrue or false
intint literal or int variable
decimaldecimal or int literal
stringstring literal. No interpolation.
textstring literal. Interpolation permitted. A bare variable name is also permitted and becomes ${name}.
enuma constant from the parameter, for example TURN_ON
flagsa list of constants, for example [MON, FRI], or a day group. Days of month accept ints: [1, 15]. The compiler writes a bool array of the correct length.
durationa duration literal (30s, 5m) or an int in the unit of the parameter
colora color literal (#FF0000) or an int
colorLista list of color literals
variablea variable name, optionally with a path: result or data["a"]["b"]. The compiler writes the name, a MacroDroidVariable object or a VariableWithDictionaryKeys object, as the parameter needs, and fills the companion dictionary-path field.
variableLista list of variable names
dictPathnormally filled from the companion variable argument. You can also give a list of strings.

contactcontact("Mom") or contact("Mom", "+15551234567")
contactList[contact("Mom"), contact("Dad")]

objectan object literal. See the fields of the parameter.

rawObjectan object literal that the compiler copies with no checks
httpParamsan object literal {"Header": "value"}. The compiler writes [{paramName, paramValue}].

blockRefLista list of block(...) or null

Action blocks

An action block is a reusable list of actions. Write it in its own file with @actionBlock. Use in and out to declare its inputs and outputs.

Call the block from a macro with callBlock. The name must be the same as the @name of the block file.

Compiler output rules

  • Output wrapper: {"macroExportVersion": 1, "macro": {...}, "globalVariables": [...], "userIcons": null}.
  • macro.m_GUID is 0. macro.aiGenerated is 1. macro.m_completed is true. These tell MacroDroid to replace placeholder IDs at import.
  • m_SIGUID is 0 on every item, except items that something references. Those get 11223344556677 followed by a counter: 112233445566771, 112233445566772.
  • Called action blocks go in macro.exportedActionBlocks. Each block gets a placeholder GUID. ActionBlockAction.actionBlockId uses the same value.
  • The root globalVariables array is always empty. A global variable must already exist on the phone.
  • Local variables go in macro.localVariables. Never write m_localVariables.
  • Every trigger, action and constraint has m_classType and m_SIGUID.
  • Always write required parameters, also when the value is 0 or false. Leave out optional parameters that hold their default value. Do not write an empty m_constraintList on items.
  • Always write m_actionList and m_triggerList on the macro, also when they are empty.
  • Key names and enum values must match the schema exactly. They are case-sensitive.
  • Escape double quotes and backslashes in every JSON string value.

Reserved words

variables triggers constraints actions if else while do repeat for break continue return true false null as when global secure in out bool int string decimal dict array color sys

A command name that is the same as a reserved word gets the suffix Of. Example: ElseAction is elseOf. Commands of that type are syntax only.

Design decisions

These points are not clear from the schema alone. Each one is settled by real MacroDroid exports or by a language rule.

QuestionAnswerSource
Magic text form for dictionary and array entries{lv=name[key]} and {v=name[key][sub]}. Keys can hold magic text: {v=Devices[{iterator_array_index}][Name]}.Real exports
What closes IterateDictionaryActionEndLoopAction.Real exports: 15 of 15 uses
SetVariableAction.dictionaryOrArrayType codes0 bool, 1 int, 2 string, 3 decimal, -1 not an entry. The codes are the same as MacroDroidVariableConstraint.dictionaryType.Real exports (0 and 2 seen with boolean and string values) and the schema enum
Format of nested dict and array entriesAn entry whose variable is {"type": "Dictionary", "entries": [...], "isArray": ...}.Real exports and the schema DictionaryEntry format
CompareValueConstraint with dict and array valuestype 4 or 5, value1 is the variable as magic text ({lv=d}), comparisonType 6 to 9.Real exports: 44 uses of comparisonType 6 and 7 on arrays
Initial value of a color variableNot permitted. Assign the color in the actions block with SetVariableAction.m_newStringValue, which the schema documents for color variables.Design rule
Import of global variables that already exist on the phoneThe compiler never exports global variables, so an import cannot change them. MacroDroid's own exports of macros that use globals also leave globalVariables empty.Design rule, matches real exports

cellConnectionTypeChange

CellConnectionTypeChangeTriggertrigger
cellConnectionTypeChange(typeOptions: flags, minimumDurationSeconds?: duration (s), subscriptionId?: int)

Triggers when the mobile (cellular) data connection type changes, e.g. LTE to 5G. Requires Android 11+. Magic text {cell_connection_type_new} (new) and {cell_connection_type_previous} (old) contain the fixed values 2G, 3G, LTE, 5G NSA, 5G SA or None. 5G NSA (non-standalone, 5G over an LTE core) is how most carriers deliver 5G; 5G SA is pure standalone 5G, so a macro that wants "any 5G" should enable both. None means no mobile data connection (e.g. airplane mode or no signal). Note the magic text value is the bare word None, not the option label 'None (no mobile data connection)'. Requires phone state permission.

ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription
typeOptions
positionaloptional
flags[true, true, true, true, true, true]typeOptionsWhich new connection types fire the trigger: [2G, 3G, LTE, 5G NSA, 5G SA, None (no mobile data connection)]
  • _2G02G
  • _3G13G
  • LTE2LTE
  • _5G_NSA35G NSA
  • _5G_SA45G SA
  • NONE5None (no mobile data connection)
minimumDurationSeconds
optional
duration (s)0minimumDurationSecondsSeconds the new connection type must remain in place before the trigger fires. 0 = fire immediately on change. Any further change within this period resets the timer.
subscriptionId
optional
int-1subscriptionIdSIM subscription ID to filter by. -1 = any SIM (default). On multi-SIM devices, use the subscription ID of the specific SIM card to monitor.

dataUsed

DataUsedTriggertrigger
dataUsed(
    networkType: enum,
    thresholdAmount?: decimal,
    thresholdUnit: enum,
    useVariableThreshold?: bool,
    thresholdVariableName?: variable,
    variableThresholdUnit?: enum,
    periodKind: enum,
    rollingAmount?: int,
    rollingUnitMinutes?: enum,
    calendarScope?: enum,
    billingDay?: int,
    cooldownMinutes?: duration (min)
)

Fires when cellular or Wi-Fi data used over a configurable period crosses (transitions from below to at-or-above) a threshold. The poll rate and exact-alarm option are GLOBAL app settings (Settings → Data Used) shared across every DataUsedTrigger; a single AlarmManager alarm runs while at least one trigger is enabled. For calendar periods the trigger auto re-arms when the period rolls over (e.g. on the billing day). For rolling windows, cooldownMinutes prevents repeat fires (default = period length). Requires Usage Access permission. On Android 9 and below, reading cellular usage also requires the Phone (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission.

Schema notes
  • This is a TRIGGER. It fires only on UPWARD crossings. To gate macro execution on the current data-used value without an event, use DataUsedConstraint in m_constraintList instead. Poll rate and useAlarm are NOT per-trigger fields - they are global preferences.

networkTransportChange

NetworkTransportChangeTriggertrigger
networkTransportChange(transportOptions: flags)

Triggers when the transport of the active (default) network changes (e.g. Android switches between Wi-Fi and cellular, even if both stay connected). While a VPN is active the transport stays VPN, and a change of the transport beneath the VPN (e.g. Wi-Fi disabled, VPN moves to cellular) also fires. Magic text {network_transport} (new), {network_transport_previous} (old) and {network_transport_underlying} (transport beneath a VPN) contain the fixed values Wi-Fi, Cellular, Ethernet, VPN or None. {network_transport_previous} may additionally contain Other (a transport that is none of the above, e.g. Bluetooth tethering); Other never fires the trigger, so it cannot be selected as a transport to match. Note the magic text value for no network is the bare word None, not the option label 'None (no network)'. Does not require location permissions.

ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription
transportOptions
positionaloptional
flags[true, true, true, true, true]transportOptionsWhich new transports fire the trigger: [Wi-Fi, Cellular, Ethernet, VPN, None (no network)]
  • WI_FI0Wi-Fi
  • CELLULAR1Cellular
  • ETHERNET2Ethernet
  • VPN3VPN
  • NONE4None (no network)

sensor

SensorTriggertrigger
sensor(
    sensorType: int,
    sensorName?: string,
    componentIndex: int,
    comparisonOption: enum,
    triggerValue: string,
    triggerValueMax?: string,
    updateMode: enum,
    checkIntervalSeconds?: duration (s)
)

Triggers when a value reported by a chosen device sensor crosses a defined threshold. Edge-triggered - fires once when the value crosses the threshold and re-arms only after the value moves back past the threshold. Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion and step detector are not. For multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) one component of the reading is tested, using the same component names as SensorReadAction dictionary keys (x, y, z, azimuth, pitch, roll, value0...). 3-axis sensors additionally support componentIndex -2 = magnitude sqrt(x²+y²+z²), useful for orientation-independent movement detection. The value that fired the trigger is available via the [sensor_value] magic text and the name of the sensor via [sensor_type]. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+. Continuous mode pauses in deep sleep; periodic mode samples via alarms and works with the screen off.

ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription
sensorType
required
intsensorTypeAndroid Sensor.TYPE_* constant of the sensor to monitor (e.g. 5=light, 8=proximity, 6=pressure, 13=ambient temperature, 12=relative humidity, 1=accelerometer, 4=gyroscope, 2=magnetic field)
sensorName
optional
stringsensorNameExact sensor name used to disambiguate when multiple sensors share a type; falls back to the default sensor of that type
componentIndex
required
intcomponentIndexIndex of the reading component to test (0 for single-value sensors; 0=x, 1=y, 2=z for 3-axis sensors; -2 = magnitude of a 3-axis reading)
comparisonOption
required
enumcomparisonOptionCondition that fires the trigger; 2 fires when the value enters the range [triggerValue, triggerValueMax] (inclusive) and re-arms when it leaves
  • INCREASES_ABOVE0Increases above
  • DECREASES_BELOW1Decreases below
  • IS_WITHIN_RANGE2Is within range
triggerValue
required
stringtriggerValueThreshold value as a string (the range minimum when comparisonOption is 2); supports magic text such as {v=my_var}
triggerValueMax
optional
stringtriggerValueMaxRange maximum as a string; only used when comparisonOption is 2; supports magic text
updateMode
required
enumupdateModeContinuous evaluates every sensor update (higher battery, pauses in deep sleep); Periodic samples once per checkIntervalSeconds via an alarm (works screen-off)
  • CONTINUOUS0Continuous
  • PERIODIC1Periodic
checkIntervalSeconds
optional
duration (s)checkIntervalSecondsSampling interval in seconds for periodic mode (minimum 10, default 30); ignored in continuous mode

systemTime

SystemTimeTriggertrigger
systemTime(
    timestamp: int,
    useMilliseconds?: bool,
    varName?: variable,
    dontUseAlarm?: bool
)

Triggers at an absolute system time given as a Unix epoch timestamp (seconds or milliseconds). The timestamp can be a fixed value or read from an integer variable; when the variable's value changes the scheduled wakeup is automatically rescheduled. If the timestamp is in the past nothing is scheduled and the trigger will not fire. One-shot - after firing it will not fire again until the variable value changes to a new future timestamp. Use TimerTrigger for clock times and RegularIntervalTrigger for repeating intervals.

Schema notes
  • Pro version only. URL format: https://ask.macrodroid.com/{device_id}/{identifier}. Same delivery model as WebHookTrigger but can respond synchronously to the caller. Exposes {webhook_caller_ip} and {webhook_query_params} magic text for use in downstream actions/constraints (same as WebHookTrigger). For deferred replies, leave sendResponse off and use the Send Webhook Response action later in the macro. Values starting with 0 (like phone numbers) are preserved as strings to avoid losing leading zeros.

Schema notes
  • Uses WirelessState enum values for m_btState. For "Device Connected" / "Device Not Connected" modes, multiple devices can be selected via m_deviceNameList (matched by OR). When m_excludeDevices is true the list is treated as the set of devices to *exclude* (so the constraint matches any device EXCEPT those listed). The legacy single-device fields (m_deviceName / m_deviceAddress / m_deviceAlias / m_anyDevice) are still honoured when m_deviceNameList is empty (backwards compatibility).

DataUsedConstraintconstraint

)

Check whether cellular or Wi-Fi data used over a configurable period exceeds (or is below) a threshold. Requires Usage Access permission. On Android 9 and below, reading cellular usage also requires the Phone (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission. To FIRE on a threshold crossing, use DataUsedTrigger instead.

Schema notes
  • This is a CONSTRAINT - it checks current data usage. It goes ONLY in m_constraintList, NEVER in m_triggerList. The threshold can be a fixed value or read from a variable. The period can be a rolling window (e.g. last 24 hours) OR a calendar period (today/this week/this month with optional billing day).

FaceUpDownConstraintconstraint

Check device physical orientation (face up, face down, vertical, sideways, in pocket). Also covers "flip device" scenarios - there is no separate FlipDeviceConstraint.

Schema notes
  • This is a CONSTRAINT, not a trigger. To detect face-down/up EVENTS, use FlipDeviceTrigger. FaceUpDownConstraint only goes in m_constraintList, NEVER in m_triggerList.

sensorValue

SensorValueConstraintconstraint
sensorValue(
    sensorType: int,
    sensorName?: string,
    componentIndex: int,
    comparisonOption: enum,
    comparisonValue: string,
    comparisonValueMax?: string
)

Only allows the macro to run when the current value reported by a chosen device sensor meets the defined condition. The sensor is read at the moment the constraint is checked (blocking up to 1 second, with a 2 second reading cache); if the sensor does not respond in time or is not present the constraint is not satisfied. Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors). For multi-value sensors one component of the reading is tested, using the same component names as SensorReadAction dictionary keys (x, y, z, azimuth, pitch, roll, value0...). 3-axis sensors additionally support componentIndex -2 = magnitude sqrt(x²+y²+z²). Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+.

ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription
sensorType
required
intsensorTypeAndroid Sensor.TYPE_* constant of the sensor to check (e.g. 5=light, 8=proximity, 6=pressure, 13=ambient temperature, 12=relative humidity, 1=accelerometer, 4=gyroscope, 2=magnetic field)
sensorName
optional
stringsensorNameExact sensor name used to disambiguate when multiple sensors share a type; falls back to the default sensor of that type
componentIndex
required
intcomponentIndexIndex of the reading component to test (0 for single-value sensors; 0=x, 1=y, 2=z for 3-axis sensors; -2 = magnitude of a 3-axis reading)
comparisonOption
required
enumcomparisonOptionCondition the current value must meet; 2 checks value is within [comparisonValue, comparisonValueMax] (inclusive)
  • GREATER_THAN0Greater than
  • LESS_THAN1Less than
  • IS_WITHIN_RANGE2Is within range
comparisonValue
required
stringcomparisonValueComparison value as a string (the range minimum when comparisonOption is 2); supports magic text such as {v=my_var}
comparisonValueMax
optional
stringcomparisonValueMaxRange maximum as a string; only used when comparisonOption is 2; supports magic text

actionBlock

ActionBlockActionaction
actionBlock(
    actionBlockId: int,
    actionBlockName: string,
    inputVarsMap: object,
    outputVarsMap: object,
    continueActionsWithoutWaiting?: bool,
    inputDictionaryMap?: object,
    outputDictionaryMap?: object
)

Invoke action block with no variable mappings - still requires empty maps

Short form: callBlock("Block Name", inputs: {...}, outputs: {...}).

Schema notes
  • Allows running reusable action blocks. Can pass input variables and receive output variables. Can run synchronously (wait) or asynchronously (continue without waiting). IMPORTANT: inputVarsMap and outputVarsMap are REQUIRED - use {} if no variables needed.
ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription
actionBlockId
required
intactionBlockIdGUID of the action block to invoke (must match m_GUID in exportedActionBlocks)
actionBlockName
required
stringactionBlockNameAction block name (for display/fallback lookup)
inputVarsMap
required
objectinputVarsMapREQUIRED - Map of action block input variable names to values/magic text. Use {} if no inputs
outputVarsMap
required
objectoutputVarsMapREQUIRED - Map of action block output variable names to local variable names. Use {} if no outputs
continueActionsWithoutWaiting
optional
boolfalsecontinueActionsWithoutWaitingIf true, continue executing next actions without waiting for action block to complete
inputDictionaryMap
optional
objectinputDictionaryMapDictionary keys for input variables that are dictionaries/arrays
outputDictionaryMap
optional
objectoutputDictionaryMapDictionary keys for output variables that are dictionaries/arrays

cameraNotificationCircle

CameraNotificationCircleActionaction
cameraNotificationCircle(
    option: enum,
    timeoutSeconds?: duration (s),
    colors?: color list,
    progressMode?: bool,
    progressVariableName?: variable,
    horizontalPositionPercent?: decimal,
    verticalPositionPercent?: int,
    circleWidthDp?: int,
    circleHeightDp?: int,
    thicknessDp?: int,
    featherEffect?: decimal,
    alpha?: decimal,
    drawOverSystemApps?: bool
)

Display a notification circle overlay around the camera area with animated gradient colors

Schema notes
  • Colors are Android color integers (e.g., -65536 = red, -16711936 = green, -16776961 = blue)
  • Use 0xFFRRGGBB as signed int for hex colors
  • Common colors: Red=-65536, Green=-16711936, Blue=-16776961, Yellow=-256, Cyan=-16711681, Magenta=-65281
  • Position values are percentages of screen dimensions (0-100)
  • Default position (90%, 3%) is typical for front cameras in top-right corner
  • Progress indicator mode (progressMode=true): draws a single fixed-colour ring that fills from the top clockwise in proportion to a linked integer/decimal variable expected in the range 0-100. In this mode only the first entry of colors is used, feather/timeout are ignored, and the ring stays visible (monitoring the variable live) until a Clear action runs.

checkImageOnScreen

CheckImageOnScreenActionaction
checkImageOnScreen(
    useStaticImage?: bool,
    imageFileUri?: string,
    imageDisplayName?: string,
    useAllFilesAccess?: bool,
    pathUri?: string,
    pathName?: string,
    filename?: string,
    allFilesAccessPath?: string,
    restrictToRegion?: bool,
    regionX?: int,
    regionY?: int,
    regionWidth?: int,
    regionHeight?: int,
    regionXVarName?: variable,
    regionYVarName?: variable,
    regionWidthVarName?: variable,
    regionHeightVarName?: variable,
    usePercentForRegion?: bool,
    matchSensitivity?: int,
    useGreyscale?: bool,
    matchResolution?: int,
    booleanResultVarName: variable,
    dictionaryOutVarName?: variable
)

Captures a screenshot and checks if a specified reference image is present on the screen using OpenCV template matching. Useful for detecting when a specific button or UI element appears (e.g. in a game). Optionally saves match location and bounds to a dictionary variable so they can be used with a Click action.

Schema notes
  • Requires accessibility service permission (for screenshot capture)
  • Requires Android 11 (API 30) or later. On older versions the action logs an error, sets the boolean result to false and the macro continues
  • Requires OpenCV library to be downloaded on first use (~15MB one-time download)
  • The reference image should be a cropped screenshot of the element to find
  • For game automation, pair with a UI Interaction click action using centerX/centerY from the dictionary variable
  • When restrictToRegion is true, coordinates are relative to the full screen (not the region)
  • Match sensitivity presets map to OpenCV TM_CCOEFF_NORMED thresholds
  • The dictionary outputs center point, bounding rectangle (start/end corners), a formatted bounds string, and match quality percentage
  • Coordinates are provided even when the boolean result is false, as long as the match confidence exceeds the minimum threshold (70%)
  • "Static image" mode uses SAF file picker only. "Dynamic image" mode offers two sub-options: SAF (folder + filename with magic text) or All Files Access (single path with magic text)
ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription
useStaticImage
optional
boolfalseuseStaticImagetrue = use a static image file (SAF), false = use a dynamic path
imageFileUri
optional
stringimageFileUriSAF URI of the reference image file (when useStaticImage=true)
imageDisplayName
optional
stringimageDisplayNameDisplay name of the selected image file
useAllFilesAccess
optional
boolfalseuseAllFilesAccessWhen useStaticImage=false: true = All Files Access mode, false = SAF folder+filename mode (default false)
pathUri
optional
stringpathUriSAF tree URI for the folder (when useStaticImage=false and useAllFilesAccess=false)
pathName
optional
stringpathNameDisplay name of the selected folder
filename
optional
stringfilenameFilename within the SAF folder, supports magic text (when useStaticImage=false and useAllFilesAccess=false)
allFilesAccessPath
optional
stringallFilesAccessPathFull file path, supports magic text (when useStaticImage=false and useAllFilesAccess=true)
restrictToRegion
optional
boolfalserestrictToRegionRestrict search to a specific screen region (default false)
regionX
optional
intregionXX coordinate of search region top-left corner
regionY
optional
intregionYY coordinate of search region top-left corner
regionWidth
optional
intregionWidthWidth of search region
regionHeight
optional
intregionHeightHeight of search region
regionXVarName
optional
variableregionXVarNameVariable name for region X (overrides regionX) A path such as regionXVarName["k"] fills booleanResultVarKeys.
regionYVarName
optional
variableregionYVarNameVariable name for region Y (overrides regionY) A path such as regionYVarName["k"] fills dictionaryOutVarKeys.
regionWidthVarName
optional
variableregionWidthVarNameVariable name for region width (overrides regionWidth)
regionHeightVarName
optional
variableregionHeightVarNameVariable name for region height (overrides regionHeight)
usePercentForRegion

boolfalseusePercentForRegionUse percentage (0-100) instead of pixels for region bounds
matchSensitivity
optional
intmatchSensitivity0=Exact(0.97), 1=High(0.88), 2=Medium(0.76), 3=Low(0.62). Default 1 (High)
useGreyscale
optional
boolfalseuseGreyscaleConvert images to greyscale before matching. Faster and more robust to color variations, but cannot distinguish elements that differ only by color. Default false
matchResolution
optional
intmatchResolution0=Full resolution, 1=Half resolution (2x downscale), 2=Quarter resolution (4x downscale). Lower resolution is faster but less precise. Coordinates are scaled back to full resolution. Default 1 (Half)

positionalrequired
variablebooleanResultVarNameBoolean variable to store whether image was found (true/false). Can be a dictionary/array variable when combined with booleanResultVarKeys

dictionaryOutVarKeys
from regionYVarName
dict pathdictionaryOutVarKeysDictionary keys for output variable

ElseIfConditionActionactionWrite with syntax
elseIfCondition(constraintList: condition, isOrCondition?: bool, dontLogIfConditionIsFalse?: bool)

Else If condition check - executes child actions if conditions are met and previous If/ElseIf was false

Do not call this as a function. Write } else if (condition) { ... }. The compiler emits ElseIfConditionAction.

Schema notes
  • Must be placed between an IfConditionAction and EndIfAction. Uses constraints to evaluate conditions. IMPORTANT: ElseIfConditionAction does NOT close the If block. The entire chain still requires a final EndIfAction. No matter how many ElseIf branches exist, there must be exactly ONE EndIfAction at the end: IfConditionAction -> [ElseIfConditionAction]... -> [ElseAction] -> EndIfAction

dontLogIfConditionIsFalse
optional
boolfalsedontLogIfConditionIsFalsecondition evaluates to false

getDataUsed

GetDataUsedActionaction
getDataUsed(
    networkType: enum,
    unit: enum,
    periodKind: enum,
    rollingAmount?: int,
    rollingUnitMinutes?: enum,
    calendarScope?: enum,
    billingDay?: int,
    variableName: variable
)

Read cellular or Wi-Fi data used over a configurable period and store it into a numeric variable. Integer target variables receive the floored whole-unit value; decimal target variables receive the value rounded to 2 decimal places. Requires Usage Access permission. On Android 9 and below, reading cellular usage also requires the Phone (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission.

Schema notes
  • This is an ACTION - it goes in m_actionList. The target variable must already exist as an Integer or Decimal variable. Use a Decimal variable when the unit is GB to keep precision (otherwise small usage rounds to 0). To CONSTRAIN macro execution on data used, use DataUsedConstraint. To FIRE on threshold crossings, use DataUsedTrigger.
ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription
networkType
required
enumnetworkTypeWhich network to measure
  • CELLULAR0Cellular
  • WI_FI1Wi-Fi
unit
required
enumunitUnit the value is written in
  • KB0KB
  • MB1MB
  • GB2GB

required

  • CALENDAR1Calendar

optional

  • MINUTES1Minutes
  • HOURS60Hours
  • DAYS1440Days

optional

  • TODAY0Today
  • THIS_WEEK1This week
  • THIS_MONTH2This month
billingDay
optional
intbillingDayDay of month the billing cycle begins (1-31). Days 29-31 wrap to the last day of months that don't have them (e.g. 31 → Feb 28/29). Used when periodKind=1 and calendarScope=2 Range 1-31

  • IMPORTANT: MacroDroid uses a FLAT action list. Actions between IfConditionAction and EndIfAction are siblings in the same m_actionList array. Do NOT nest m_actionList within IfConditionAction. Requires matching EndIfAction. Use ElseAction for else branch. m_constraintList MUST contain at least one constraint - empty means always-true (Else never executes). Extends ConditionAction which has m_constraintList and m_isOrCondition (inherited from Action base class). CRITICAL - m_constraintList MUST ONLY contain CONSTRAINT classTypes (names ending in "Constraint"). NEVER put trigger classTypes (names ending in "Trigger") in m_constraintList - they will not work. Common mistake: using FlipDeviceTrigger in m_constraintList instead of FaceUpDownConstraint. If you need to check a state/condition, find the matching CONSTRAINT class, not a trigger. WRONG: m_constraintList: [{"m_classType": "FlipDeviceTrigger", ...}] (trigger in constraint list!) RIGHT: m_constraintList: [{"m_classType": "FaceUpDownConstraint", ...}] (correct constraint) CRITICAL - EndIfAction REQUIRED: Every If/ElseIf chain MUST end with exactly one EndIfAction. This applies even when using ElseIfConditionAction chains. A common mistake is to omit EndIfAction after the last ElseIf or Else branch. CORRECT pattern: IfConditionAction -> ElseIfConditionAction -> ElseAction -> EndIfAction WRONG (crashes): IfConditionAction -> ElseIfConditionAction -> ElseAction (missing EndIfAction)
ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription

boolfalsedontLogIfConditionIsFalsecondition evaluates to false

java(

    consoleVariableName?: variable,

Execute Java/Kotlin code (BeanShell interpreter)

Schema notes
  • Uses BeanShell interpreter. Code runs in a sandbox with access to MacroDroid context. Built-in script bindings: 'appContext' (application Context), 'magicText' (evaluateString/evaluateInt/evaluateBoolean/evaluateDecimal), 'variableSetter' (set MacroDroid variables - setString/setInt/setDecimal/setBoolean/setColor (hex string or packed ARGB integer)/setArray/setDict, each optionally taking a String[] of dictionary keys and/or a create-if-not-exist flag 1=Local 2=Global; in setArray/setDict JSON, a string value with a leading # (#RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB) only becomes a colour entry if it replaces an existing colour entry, otherwise it stays a string and for dictionaries a companion '<key>ColorVar' colour entry is added alongside it), 'globals' (share objects across scripts), 'accessibility' (facade exposing the full standard AccessibilityService API - all public AccessibilityService methods e.g. getRootInActiveWindow/getWindows/findFocus/performGlobalAction/getSystemActions/dispatchGesture/getServiceInfo/setServiceInfo/ getMagnificationController/getSoftKeyboardController/getFingerprintGestureController/getAccessibilityButtonController/takeScreenshot/ setGestureDetectionPassthroughRegion/setTouchExplorationPassthroughRegion/attachAccessibilityOverlayToDisplay - but NO MacroDroid-specific methods; also isAvailable() and getContext() which returns the live accessibility service as a Context (null if none connected). 'accessibility' is itself a Context (it wraps the live accessibility service), so all inherited Context methods can be called directly on it (getSystemService/getResources/getPackageName/getContentResolver/startActivity/...) e.g. a WindowManager that can add TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY windows; MacroDroid-specific service methods are NOT exposed; version-gated methods no-op on older Android versions; requires the MacroDroid or UI Interaction accessibility service to be enabled), 'activityHelper' (startActivityForResult(intent, timeoutMs) blocking - requires runInBackgroundThread=true; withActivity(callback) runs code with a transparent Activity that the script must finish()).

javaScript

JavaScriptActionaction
javaScript(
    scriptText: text,
    blockNextAction?: bool,
    stringVariableName?: variable,
    consoleVariableName?: variable,
    javascriptEngine?: string
)

Execute JavaScript code

Schema notes
  • Supports multiple JavaScript engines
  • Scripts can set MacroDroid variables via setVariable(name, value), with the type detected from the value (string/number/boolean/array/object). Optional third argument is a key-path array for setting an element inside a dictionary or array, e.g. setVariable(\"dict\", \"val\", [\"key\"]). Optional fourth argument forces creation if the variable does not exist: \"local\" or \"global\" (pass null for keys if unused), e.g. setVariable(\"newVar\", 5, null, \"global\"). When the target variable (or targeted dictionary entry) is a colour, a hex string (#RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB) or packed ARGB integer value is coerced to a colour. When setting a whole array/object, a string value with a leading # (#RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB) only becomes a colour entry if it replaces an existing colour entry; otherwise it stays a string and (for objects) a companion '<key>ColorVar' colour entry is added alongside it. Supported on the JetPack JavascriptEngine, QuickJS and Rhino engines (not JSEvaluator).
  • Magic text can be evaluated to a typed value via magicText.evaluateInt/evaluateString/evaluateDecimal/evaluateBoolean with a literal magic text string, e.g. magicText.evaluateInt(\"{battery}\"). Standard magic text elsewhere in the script is still replaced once at the start.
  • Objects can be shared globally across script runs (and with Java actions) via globals.set/get/has/remove/clearAll/listAll, e.g. globals.set(\"key\", value) then globals.get(\"key\"). Reads see the values present at script start; writes are persisted after the script finishes. Supported on the JetPack JavascriptEngine, QuickJS and Rhino engines (not JSEvaluator).

LoopActionactionWrite with syntax
loop(
    option: enum,
    fixedOptionCount?: int,
    fixedOptionVariable?: variable,
    timedDurationValue?: int,
    timedTimeUnit?: enum,

Repeat actions a specified number of times, until a condition is met, or for a period of time

Do not call this as a function. Write while (...) { }, do { } while (...);, repeat (n) { }, repeat (duration) { }, while (true) { }. The compiler emits LoopAction.

Schema notes
  • Requires matching EndLoopAction. Place all actions to repeat between LoopAction and EndLoopAction. Structure in m_actionList: [LoopAction, ...actions to repeat..., EndLoopAction] Supports fixed count, variable count, while-do, do-while, endless, and timed loops. For polling/retry loops (waiting for an app to close, a variable to change, etc.) either make the state the While-Do condition (m_option=1 with the constraint in m_constraintList) or, in a fixed-count/timed loop, check it each iteration with IfConditionAction + BreakFromLoopAction so the loop exits immediately rather than spinning for the full count/duration. For timed loops (m_option=4), the loop records a start timestamp and exits once the specified duration has elapsed. Magic text {loop_iteration} resolves to the 1-based number of the currently executing iteration of the innermost active loop (any loop type), i.e. 1 on the first pass through to N on the last pass of a loop that runs N times. Resolves to -1 when used outside any loop. The {loop_iteration} magic text option only appears in the magic text picker for actions nested inside a loop/iterator.

readSoundLevel

ReadSoundLevelActionaction
readSoundLevel(
    audioSourceOption: enum,
    captureLengthText?: text,
    maxVariableName?: variable,
    averageVariableName?: variable,
    minVariableName?: variable
)

Measure the sound level from an audio input (microphone by default) for a set period and save the maximum, average and/or minimum level into number variables. Levels are in dB relative to the maximum input level (dBFS), so 0 dB is the loudest possible value and silence is around -96 dB (louder sounds give values closer to 0). Blocks until the capture period has elapsed and the variables have been set. At least one output variable must be set (users usually only need the maximum). Requires the record audio permission.

samsungRoutines

SamsungRoutinesActionaction
samsungRoutines(
    routineName: text,
    actionMode?: enum,
    endPreviousBeforeStart?: bool,
    routineUuid?: int
)

Invoke a Samsung Modes & Routines manual routine (Samsung devices only)

Schema notes
  • The app picks one of three runtime modes by probing device capability (not the app version): LEGACY: content providers respond → routine controlled by name via content provider; actionMode (Start/Stop/Toggle) and endPreviousBeforeStart honoured; routineName supports magic text. SHORTCUT (One UI 8.5 / Routines v5+): providers blocked but a CREATE_SHORTCUT picker exists → routine picked interactively so its UUID is captured, then launched via ShortcutLaunchActivity which always TOGGLES (actionMode/endPreviousBeforeStart ignored); magic text / free-text name NOT supported; actions configured before the lockdown (no routineUuid) must be reconfigured. BLOCKED (One UI 8.0 / Routines 4.9): providers are signature-walled (READ_ROUTINE_INFO became a signature permission) AND there is no picker → no third-party mechanism remains. The action cannot run on this device, shows a warning, and is skipped (logged) at runtime. There is currently no workaround.
ParameterKindDefaultJSON fieldDescription
routineName
positionalrequired
text ${}routineNameManual routine name (legacy versions only; on Samsung Routines v5+ this is set by the picker and not user-editable)
actionMode
optional
enumSTARTactionModeAction to perform (ignored on Samsung Routines v5+; always toggles there)
  • START0Start
  • STOP1Stop
  • TOGGLE2Toggle
endPreviousBeforeStart
optional
boolfalseendPreviousBeforeStartEnd the routine first then start (legacy versions only)
routineUuid

introutineUuidCaptured Samsung routine UUID, required on Routines v5+; set via the interactive picker, do not edit by hand

    additionalExtras?: object list,
    flags?: int
)

Send an Android intent (broadcast, activity, or service)

Schema notes
  • Do NOT use this to call a web API or fetch a URL. An Activity intent with android.intent.action.VIEW and an http(s) m_data just hands the URL to a browser for the user to look at, and fails with "No Activity found to handle Intent" when nothing on the device can open it. Use HttpRequestAction instead.
  • Only use m_action android.intent.action.VIEW when the intent is genuinely meant to open something on screen (a web page, a map, a document).
  • m_data must be a complete URI including scheme. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped before it is parsed.
  • Boolean extras accept true/false in any case, including the localised True/False text that boolean variables expand to (e.g. {lv=my_bool}).
  • To share a file with another app (e.g. m_action android.intent.action.SEND with m_mimeType image/*), put the file in an extra named android.intent.extra.STREAM with type 8 (URI). The value can be a file path, a file:// uri or a content:// uri (such as one from the Shared File trigger); paths are exposed to the receiving app through a content uri and read permission is granted automatically.

Perform a one-off read of a device sensor and save the result into a variable. Blocks until the sensor is read (or up to 5 seconds). Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion, step detector and heart beat are not. Single-value sensors (light, proximity, pressure, temperature, humidity, step counter, heart rate) save into a decimal variable; multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) save into a dictionary variable with named keys (e.g. x, y, z). The device orientation sensor (type 27) saves value0 = 0 portrait, 1 rotated 90 degrees, 2 upside down, 3 rotated 270 degrees, or -1 when the device is flat; if the driver does not report within 1 second the orientation is derived from the accelerometer. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+ because they require a health permission MacroDroid does not hold - do not use them in macros targeting Android 16+ devices.

Write a summary of the user's macros and/or action blocks into a dictionary variable. Each entry is keyed by macro name and contains Id, Category, Description, Favourite, Enabled, Last Edited, Last Invoked, Logging allowed, plus Triggers/Actions/Constraints arrays (each with name, configuredName, detail, enabled, constraints). Use this to inspect, count or report on the user's own macros.

Schema notes
  • Result is a dictionary keyed by macro name. Walk it with IterateDictionaryAction to count or filter; each entry's Triggers/Actions/Constraints are arrays that can themselves be iterated to count items or read each item's name/configuredName/detail.

terminateRunning

TerminateRunningActionactionWrite with syntax
terminateRunning()

Terminate ONLY the current running instance of this macro (execution stops at this action)

Do not call this as a function. Write return;. The compiler emits TerminateRunningAction.

Schema notes
  • Ends just the invocation that executes it - no subsequent actions in that instance run. It does NOT stop any other running instances of the macro (e.g. a loop started by an earlier invocation keeps running). To stop other running instances - such as an ON/OFF toggle that must stop a running loop - use CancelActiveMacroAction targeting this macro (m_GUID 111) with excludeCurrentInstance true. No serialized parameters.

No parameters.

uiInteraction

UIInteractionActionaction
uiInteraction(uiInteractionConfiguration: raw object, action: int)

Interact with UI elements (tap, click, swipe, type, press, touch, pinch zoom, rotate) or tap at screen coordinates. Replaces the legacy Touch Screen action - there is no 'TouchScreenAction'

Schema notes
  • Complex action with UiInteractionConfiguration object
  • All coordinate fields support variable names for dynamic values. Both finger paths are dispatched simultaneously with the same duration GestureSequence: startX: [int] startY: [int] xyPercentages: [bool] durationMs: [int] waitBeforeNext: [bool] gestures: [arr, "List of GestureEntry objects with endX, endY coordinates"] showTouchLocation: [bool, "Briefly draw the gesture path (line with a dot at each point and a dot animating along it to show direction) where the sequence occurs"] PinchZoom: point1X: [int, "X coordinate of first finger"] point1Y: [int, "Y coordinate of first finger"] point2X: [int, "X coordinate of second finger"] point2Y: [int, "Y coordinate of second finger"] xyPercentages: [bool, "true=percentage coordinates, false=pixel coordinates"] zoomIn: [bool, "true=zoom in (fingers converge), false=zoom out (fingers diverge)"] zoomPercent: [int, "1-100, how far to move. 100% zoom in = fingers converge to center. 100% zoom out = fingers reach screen edge"] durationMs: [int, "Duration of gesture in milliseconds"] waitBeforeNext: [bool, "Block next actions until complete"] showTouchLocation: [bool, "Briefly draw both finger paths (line with endpoint dots and a dot animating along each to show direction) where the pinch occurs"]
  • All coordinate fields support variable names for dynamic values TwoFingerRotate: point1X: [int, "X coordinate of first finger"] point1Y: [int, "Y coordinate of first finger"] point2X: [int, "X coordinate of second finger"] point2Y: [int, "Y coordinate of second finger"] xyPercentages: [bool, "true=percentage coordinates, false=pixel coordinates"] rotateDegrees: [int, "-360 to 360, positive=clockwise, negative=counter-clockwise"] durationMs: [int, "Duration of gesture in milliseconds"] waitBeforeNext: [bool, "Block next actions until complete"] showTouchLocation: [bool, "Briefly draw both finger arc paths (line with endpoint dots and a dot animating along each to show rotation direction) where the rotate occurs"]
  • Both fingers rotate around the center point between them. All coordinate fields support variable names for dynamic values Paste: useClipboard: [bool, "true=paste from clipboard, false=use custom text"] forceClear: [bool, "Clear existing text before pasting"] text: [str, "Custom text to paste (when useClipboard=false)"]

required

intactionAction type: 0=Click, 1=LongClick, 2=Copy, 3=Cut, 4=Paste, 5=ClearSelection, 6=Gesture, 7=GestureSequence, 8=PressEnter, 9=PinchZoom, 10=TwoFingerRotate

WebHook2wayResponseActionaction
webHook2wayResponse(
    option: enum,
    text?: text,
    htmlText?: text,
    responseCode?: int,
    headerParams?: headers
)

Send a deferred response back to the caller of a Webhook (with response) trigger (Pro version only)

Schema notes
  • Pro version only. Must be used in a macro invoked by WebHook2wayTrigger. Use this when the trigger has sendResponse=false so the reply can be assembled later in the macro (e.g. after a long-running action). The caller is identified via the callback info on the trigger context, so no targeting fields are needed here.
